weights.csoNote: 'Worst headache of life', thunderclap, maximal at onset ± meningism (captured here via photophobia/vomiting, as 'neck stiffness' is not a token). CT then LP for xanthochromia.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed; AHA/ASA aneurysmal SAH guidance

weights.csoNote: Uganda: bacterial (pneumococcal/meningococcal), cryptococcal (HIV) and TB meningitis; do not delay LP/antibiotics; HSV encephalitis with altered cognition/seizures. ('Neck stiffness' is not a capture token — photophobia is the proxy.)
weights.weightCitation: WHO meningitis guidance; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: in HIV the SOL is often toxoplasmosis, primary CNS lymphoma, tuberculoma or cryptococcoma. Morning headache worse on bending/coughing/lying + papilloedema + focal signs/seizures.

Made CONDITIONAL on age over 50 — GCA essentially never occurs under 50, so an unconditional pin would be noise in young patients. GCA also appears LESS common in sub-Saharan African than Northern-European populations (basePrior low). Jaw claudication and scalp tenderness (classic) are NOT capture tokens. Sight-threatening: start steroids immediately on suspicion.
weights.weightCitation: BSR Giant Cell Arteritis Guideline; ACR/EULAR GCA classification criteria; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Kept UNCONDITIONAL (Uganda is holoendemic — any febrile headache needs a malaria RDT/smear). 'Cerebral malaria' is the SEVERE subset (impaired consciousness + parasitaemia, other causes excluded) needing IV artesunate. Check GLUCOSE (hypoglycaemia mimics/coexists — DEFG) and exclude concurrent meningitis.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines for Malaria (2025); Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Recurrent, unilateral, throbbing, photophobia +/- aura. A FIRST/worst or thunderclap headache is NOT migraine until secondary causes are excluded.
Bilateral, band-like/pressing, mild-moderate, no significant nausea/photophobia — diagnosed only after excluding secondary causes.

CONDITIONAL must-not-miss (pin on HIV/immunosuppression). basePrior population-dependent — in advanced HIV (CD4<100) this is the LEADING cause of meningitis in Uganda. Subacute headache + fever, often WITHOUT classic neck stiffness; raised ICP is the killer (needs serial therapeutic LPs). Serum/CSF CrAg.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines on cryptococcal disease in HIV; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL must-not-miss (pin on HIV/immunosuppression). basePrior population-dependent — the commonest FOCAL brain lesion in advanced HIV (CD4<100). Headache + focal deficit/seizures; multiple ring-enhancing lesions on CT; empirical anti-toxoplasma trial; differential is primary CNS lymphoma / tuberculoma.
weights.weightCitation: WHO HIV/opportunistic-infection guidelines; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: The dominant trigger is the BP VALUE, captured in VITALS (a hypertensive emergency also surfaces via the vitals-escalation pack) — this entry weights the clinical encephalopathy features. Hypertensive encephalopathy is a diagnosis of EXCLUSION — exclude stroke/SAH first; PRES on imaging.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2024 / AHA hypertension guidance (BP thresholds — see vitals-escalation pack); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL must-not-miss (pin on pregnancy/reproductive-age woman) — a LEADING cause of maternal death in Uganda. Relevant in pregnancy >20wks or postpartum: headache + visual disturbance + hypertension + proteinuria; eclampsia adds seizures. Management is MgSO4 (NOT diazepam) + BP control + delivery; use MEOWS not NEWS2 in pregnancy. Gestation/proteinuria are captured via vitals/obstetric flow.
weights.weightCitation: WHO recommendations on pre-eclampsia/eclampsia; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (obstetric); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uncommon and PROTEAN — easily missed. Key risks: pregnancy/puerperium, oestrogen/OCP, dehydration, thrombophilia, and local sepsis (mastoiditis/otitis/sinusitis — only loosely captured as 'high-risk exposure'). Diagnosis needs CT/MR venography; anticoagulate EVEN if a venous haemorrhagic infarct is present.
weights.weightCitation: ESO / AHA cerebral venous sinus thrombosis guidance; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Grouped two entities. BRAIN ABSCESS = fever + focal deficit + raised ICP (from sinusitis/otitis/HIV/endocarditis) — a must-not-miss emergency. NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS (Taenia solium) = a LEADING cause of adult-onset seizures/epilepsy in pig-keeping areas of Uganda, more chronic. The pork/Taenia exposure and the ENT/endocarditis source history are not specifically tokenised.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed; WHO neurocysticercosis / Taenia solium guidance

weights.csoNote: Facial/periorbital pressure worse on bending forward, nasal symptoms, recent URTI; usually self-limiting — orbital/intracranial spread are the red flags.
weights.weightCitation: ICHD-3 (2018) (headache attributed to rhinosinusitis); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Chronic daily headache (>=15 days/month) with regular OVERUSE of acute analgesics/triptans — under-recognised. The medication-overuse history is NOT a capture token (recommend adding a current-/overused-medication field). Usually on a background of migraine/tension-type; treat by withdrawing the overused drug.
